errors.description: The braid is narrower and far more consistent down the leg than attempt 2, but has not reached the specified one twentieth. Measured on this 880x1168 render by scanning the full satin band (not just its highlight): at y=400 the leg spans 289 px and the band about 20 px (6.9%); at y=600 leg 243 px, band about 20 px (8.2%); at y=800 leg 214 px, band about 18 px (8.4%). Attempt 2 measured 7-11% and was inconsistent along the leg. So this is about 1.6x the specified 5%, which on a real trouser is a braid of roughly 2 cm against the 1.2 cm the tech pack names - still squarely inside the evening-braid range and nothing like the ceremonial stripe of attempt 1, but wider than drawn.
errors.expected: satin braid about one twentieth (5%) of the visible leg width at mid-thigh, no wider than the pressed front crease
errors.actual: consistently 7-8.4% of the visible leg width down the full length of the leg
errors.correction: narrow the braid by a further third if regenerated; the width has now been stable across two attempts at 7-8%, so the model appears to have a floor on how narrow it will render a contrast band at this resolution

errors.description: The satin braid renders as a deep glossy near-black band against the charcoal worsted - the material contrast is now unmistakable, which fixes the attempt-2 finding - but it reads darker than the surrounding cloth rather than catching light as satin normally would, so the contrast is more tonal than specular.
errors.expected: satin sheen catching the light against matte worsted
errors.actual: clearly a different material, but reading as a darker glossy band rather than a light-catching one
errors.correction: angle the lighting so the braid catches a specular highlight along its length

notes: ATTEMPT 3 vs /images/blueprints/factory/5252459c3a51__3382__Side_seam_with_fabric_1.2cm_width_.jpg. The framing is now exactly right and clean for the first time: trouser alone from the top of the waistband to just below the hem against the plain sweep, with the shoes of attempt 2 and the jacket hem of attempt 1 both gone - naming BOTH frame edges explicitly in the same correction is what finally stopped the whack-a-mole. Material contrast is also fixed: the braid now reads instantly as a different cloth. Back welt pocket and button, front pocket opening, belt loops, plain hem, leg line and taper all match the drawing, and the braid is a single continuous band exactly on the outseam. The one residual is braid width, which has now sat at 7-8% of leg width across two attempts against a 5% specification - a genuine but non-blocking deviation, and no longer capable of being confused with a wider-stripe sibling. Zero critical or major findings; retry budget spent.
